ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Eight-bit post-training quantization of VGGT with token-aware activation scales
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations using per-channel weight scales and per-tensor activation scales fitted on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Give the camera and register tokens their own scale set, since their statistics differ from image tokens. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and ScanNet held-out scenes with point map Chamfer distance on DTU, then measure peak memory and latency with batch size 1 at 518-pixel input. Fit the scales from 5 random draws of the calibration sequences and compare them.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, naive min-max 8-bit quantization, and a variant where special tokens share the image-token scales to isolate their contribution.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Token-specific scales should keep pose AUC within 1 point of full precision while the naive baseline loses several points; it might break if the special tokens interact with later layers more strongly than expected.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration-size study for post-training quantization of VGGT on two benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations with per-channel weight scales and per-tensor activation scales, fitted on calibration sets of 8 and 64 sequences from CO3Dv2, using 10 random draws per size. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K plus point map Chamfer distance on DTU. Record peak memory and latency with batch size 1 at 518-pixel input, and log the scale statistics of the camera and register tokens, then plot the spread of pose AUC between draws against the size of the calibration set.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, naive min-max 8-bit quantization, and percentile clipping for the activations.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Pose AUC should saturate once the calibration set reaches 64 sequences, with variation between draws shrinking below 0.5 points; the trend may break on scenes with unusual camera motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Smoothing the camera and register token outliers in VGGT activations
PROPOSAL: Collect activation statistics from the 1.2B VGGT on 64 CO3Dv2 sequences, listing per-channel maxima and kurtosis for image tokens versus the camera and register tokens in the global attention blocks. Apply SmoothQuant-style migration of outlier scale into the weights with strength 0.5, computed separately for the special-token channels, then quantize to 8-bit weights and activations. Evaluate pose AUC at 30 degrees and depth error on 50 held-out scenes from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet.
CONTROLS: Full-precision model, plain per-tensor 8-bit quantization, and migration with a strength shared by all tokens to test whether separate treatment matters.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Separate migration should cut the activation range of special-token channels by an order of magnitude and keep pose AUC near full precision; it could fail if the outliers live in the weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Outlier migration strength study for 8-bit VGGT and DUSt3R on two scene collections
PROPOSAL: Collect activation statistics from the 1.2B VGGT and from DUSt3R on 256 CO3Dv2 sequences and ScanNet scenes, listing per-channel maxima, kurtosis and skewness for image tokens versus the camera and register tokens in the frame and global attention blocks. Apply SmoothQuant-style migration with 5 strengths, computed from the whole set, then quantize to 8-bit weights and activations. Evaluate pose AUC at 30 degrees, depth error and point tracking accuracy on 50 held-out scenes from both collections.
CONTROLS: Full-precision models, plain per-tensor 8-bit quantization, and per-channel activation quantization on these blocks, to see which factor drives the gap.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: A strength of 0.5 should give the best pose AUC on both models, with kurtosis of the special-token channels dropping sharply; the ordering may fail to hold for DUSt3R, which has no special tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Four-bit weight quantization of VGGT with rotated attention projections
PROPOSAL: Quantize the weights of the 1.2B VGGT to 4 bits with GPTQ using a Hessian estimated from 64 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2, keeping activations at 8 bits and using group size 128. Insert orthogonal Hadamard rotations before the query, key and value projections of the global attention blocks so channel outliers spread out, and fuse them into adjacent weights at no inference cost. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K with 50 held-out scenes per dataset, together with Chamfer distance on DTU, then report weight memory in gigabytes.
CONTROLS: GPTQ without rotation, round-to-nearest 4-bit weights, and a variant rotating only the frame attention blocks to locate where rotation matters.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Rotation should recover most of the pose accuracy lost by plain 4-bit GPTQ with weight memory roughly 3.5 times smaller; it could fail on the point tracking head, whose statistics are distinct.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: GPTQ four-bit weight compression of VGGT with a Hessian sample count sweep
PROPOSAL: Quantize the weights of the 1.2B VGGT to 4 bits with GPTQ, estimating the Hessian from 16 and 256 CO3Dv2 sequences, using 8 random draws per sample count and keeping activations in 16-bit precision. Switch activation ordering on and off. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K and Chamfer distance on DTU, and report weight memory in gigabytes. Relate the output error of the attention blocks against full precision to the sample count and to the group size, taking the final global block as the reference.
CONTROLS: GPTQ with larger group sizes, round-to-nearest 4-bit weights, and a variant with 6-bit weights on the same model.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Output error of the blocks should flatten beyond 64 sequences, so more samples buy little; the curve may fail to settle if the last global blocks stay noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity-driven calibration selection for VGGT using frame embeddings
PROPOSAL: Embed 200 candidate CO3Dv2 sequences with DINOv2 features, then pick 16 calibration sequences by farthest-point selection in embedding space. Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and activations with these sequences, and compare the activation ranges they produce, special tokens included, with those from random sequences. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on a held-out set of 60 sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, and relate the spread of the results to the embedding coverage of the chosen sequences.
CONTROLS: 16 randomly sampled sequences with 5 seeds, the 16 sequences with lowest embedding diversity, and full-precision VGGT as an upper bound.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Diverse selection should give a smaller spread of pose AUC between selections than random sampling; it might not hold if embedding diversity does not track geometric difficulty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration sampling for VGGT with giant feature extractors and clustering
PROPOSAL: Embed 2000 candidate sequences from CO3Dv2 plus ScanNet with DINOv2 giant features and with CLIP features, then pick 16 calibration sequences by clustering and by determinantal sampling in both embedding spaces. Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and activations with these sequences and compare the activation ranges they produce. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on a held-out set of 60 sequences from CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K.
CONTROLS: 16 randomly sampled sequences with 3 seeds, the 16 sequences with lowest embedding diversity, and full-precision VGGT as an upper bound.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Both selectors should give a smaller spread of pose AUC than random sampling, with little difference between the two feature spaces; they may fail on ScanNet, where room scenes look alike.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Outlier-contaminated calibration pools and robust range estimation for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Build a pool of 300 sequences from CO3Dv2 and contaminate 10 percent of it with rare scenes, namely motion-blurred, dark and near-textureless captures. Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and activations with ranges estimated from 24 sequences sampled at random, sampled by embedding diversity, and sampled after dropping sequences whose activation maxima exceed the 95th percentile. Evaluate pose AUC at 30 degrees and depth error on 80 clean held-out scenes, using 3 draws per strategy.
CONTROLS: Clean-pool random sampling, full-precision VGGT, and min-max versus percentile range estimation inside the contaminated pool.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Filtering should recover most of the accuracy lost to contamination, while random sampling loses 1 to 3 points of AUC; it risks failing when blurred scenes are exactly the ones deployed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of VGGT activation ranges under calibration resampling and a smaller backbone
PROPOSAL: Take a pool of 300 CO3Dv2 sequences and sample 24-sequence calibration sets from it 20 times, then record the 8-bit activation ranges of the 1.2B VGGT for the special tokens and image tokens in 12 layers. Summarize the spread of the ranges by coefficient of variation and relate it to the pose AUC at 30 degrees that a draw yields on 80 held-out scenes. Repeat with a second model of 300M parameters and check the same layers there, to see whether the spread follows model size.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, min-max range estimation, and a pool of 100 sequences for comparison on the same layers.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Spread should be largest in the special-token channels of late layers and should predict AUC loss; the relation could fail if pose accuracy is dominated by a few layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Int8 deployment of quantized VGGT with TensorRT engines and frame counts
PROPOSAL: Export the 8-bit weight and activation VGGT to TensorRT with fused quantize-dequantize nodes, using calibration from 32 sequences from CO3Dv2. Measure latency, throughput and peak memory at 8 and 32 input frames and 518-pixel resolution, and verify that pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and Chamfer distance on DTU match the simulated quantization within 0.5 points. Profile which blocks dominate runtime after quantization.
CONTROLS: Full-precision and half-precision TensorRT engines, and simulated quantization in PyTorch as the accuracy reference.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The int8 engine should run roughly 1.8 times faster with about half the memory of half precision; the speed-up may fail to hold at 32 frames, where attention dominates and stays in higher precision.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fused quantize-dequantize Triton kernels for VGGT attention with autotuned tiles
PROPOSAL: Write fused Triton kernels that apply 8-bit quantize-dequantize inside the frame and global attention blocks of the 1.2B VGGT, and autotune 200 tile and warp configurations for the shapes seen at 8 and 32 input frames. Measure latency and peak memory at 518-pixel resolution, and verify that pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 plus ScanNet with Chamfer distance on DTU match the simulated quantization within 0.5 points.
CONTROLS: Unfused PyTorch quantization, half-precision attention using the stock kernels, and the simulated quantization reference as an accuracy check.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Fusion should remove most of the cost of unfused quantization and give about 1.5 times lower latency; autotuning may find little beyond a handful of configurations and may not beat the defaults.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer test of SmoothQuant, GPTQ and PTQ4ViT recipes to VGGT
PROPOSAL: Apply the SmoothQuant, GPTQ and PTQ4ViT recipes to the 1.2B VGGT at 8-bit and 6-bit weights and activations, calibrated on 32 sequences from CO3Dv2 with the default hyperparameters of the recipe. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 plus Chamfer distance on DTU, and examine which transformer blocks lose the most accuracy under a given recipe. The aim is to find out whether methods built for language and 2D vision work on a 3D transformer without changes.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, naive min-max quantization at the same bit-widths, and the three recipes with camera and register tokens kept in half precision.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Recipes should hold at 8 bits but degrade at 6 bits, with GPTQ and SmoothQuant retaining more pose AUC than PTQ4ViT; the camera token could make all of them fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Six-method baseline survey of quantization recipes on VGGT with four datasets
PROPOSAL: Apply the SmoothQuant, GPTQ, AWQ, OmniQuant, PTQ4ViT and PTQ4DiT recipes to the 1.2B VGGT at 8-bit and 6-bit weights and activations, calibrated on 32 CO3Dv2 sequences with default hyperparameters. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees and depth error on CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K, ScanNet plus DTU, and examine which transformer blocks lose the most accuracy under a given recipe. The aim is to find out whether methods built for language and 2D vision work on a 3D transformer.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, naive min-max quantization at the same bit-widths, and per-token activation quantization on the same blocks.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Weight-only recipes should hold at 6 bits while activation recipes degrade, and the ranking should stay stable between datasets; the camera token may break every method alike.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does keeping camera and register tokens in higher precision matter for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and activations with 24 CO3Dv2 calibration sequences, and vary the treatment of the camera and register tokens: quantized like image tokens, kept in 16-bit activations, or given separate 8-bit scales. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and ScanNet plus depth error on DTU, and estimate the memory and latency cost of the higher-precision path with batch size 1. Inspect the attention weights those tokens receive in blocks 12 and 23 before and after quantization.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, uniform 8-bit quantization with no special handling, and a variant that leaves the attention logits in higher precision.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Higher precision for those tokens should recover most of the pose loss at under 2 percent extra latency; it might not hold if the tokens carry little pose information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Block sensitivity of VGGT to 8-bit activation quantization on three datasets
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations with 24 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2, leaving the attention blocks in 16-bit precision one at a time while the others are quantized, with 3 seeds for the calibration draw. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K and ScanNet, and record DTU depth error for the full set of runs. Rank blocks by recovered accuracy, and relate the ranking to the kurtosis of the input activations of a block, shown for blocks 12 and 23.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, uniform 8-bit quantization of all blocks, and random choices of blocks to keep in higher precision.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: A handful of early global blocks should account for most of the recovered accuracy; the ranking may shift between datasets, and kurtosis may not predict it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Six-bit quantization of VGGT with multi-task evaluation including point tracking
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 6-bit weights and 6-bit activations with token-specific scales and diversity-selected calibration of 32 sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and RealEstate10K, depth error and Chamfer distance on DTU, and tracking accuracy on TAP-Vid. Report memory and latency at batch size 1, and compare the accuracy drop per task against full precision.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, min-max 6-bit quantization, and the same method without token-specific scales; calibration sampled at random with 3 seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Pose and depth should stay within 2 percent of full precision while tracking degrades most; the method may degrade at 6 bits if heavy tails remain in the value projections.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Depth robustness of six-bit VGGT to calibration draws and frame counts
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2B VGGT to 6-bit weights and 6-bit activations with token-specific scales, fitted from 32 CO3Dv2 calibration sequences in 8 independent random draws. Measure depth error on DTU at 2, 8 and 48 input frames, together with peak memory and latency at batch size 1. Compare the accuracy drop per frame count against full precision and fit its trend against the number of frames for the 8 draws.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, min-max 6-bit quantization, and the same method fitted with calibration from only 8 sequences.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The drop should grow slowly with frame count and vary by under 1 percent between draws; it might show a jump beyond 32 frames where context length exceeds training and the fit may break.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Percentile clipping against error-minimizing ranges for VGGT activations
PROPOSAL: Compare four activation range estimators for the 1.2B VGGT at 8-bit weights and activations: min-max, percentile clipping, mean-squared-error search and entropy-based selection. Fit each on calibration sets of 16 and 64 sequences from CO3Dv2, with 3 draws per set size. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and ScanNet plus Chamfer distance on DTU, and report how much the chosen clipping threshold differs between draws for the camera token channels.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, per-token dynamic activation quantization as a calibration-free comparison, and min-max applied only to image tokens.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Error-minimizing search should win at 16 sequences and the gap should narrow at 64; clipping thresholds for the camera token may remain unstable between draws and fail to converge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Block-wise reconstruction of VGGT quantization parameters with learned rounding
PROPOSAL: Refine the 8-bit weight rounding and activation scales of the 1.2B VGGT block by block, minimizing output error against the full-precision block on 128 CO3Dv2 calibration sequences for 1000 iterations in the style of AdaRound and BRECQ. Evaluate camera pose AUC at 30 degrees on CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, and Chamfer distance on DTU, and track the reconstruction loss of a block during optimization.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, round-to-nearest 8-bit quantization with min-max scales, and mean-squared-error range search without learned rounding.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Learned rounding should lower block error clearly but gain under 1 point of pose AUC over range search at 8 bits; larger gains may only appear at lower bit-widths and may not show here.
